clinical_category: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse teaches a client how to use a newly prescribed antibiotic safely. Which statement by the client shows correct understanding?

options.A: I’ll take it exactly as prescribed, won’t share or save it for later, and will contact my healthcare professional if I have questions or side effects.
options.B: I’ll stop it on my own once I feel better, even if the prescribed instructions say to continue, because symptom relief means treatment is complete.
options.C: I’ll save any unused doses for another illness with similar symptoms so I can start treatment quickly without contacting a healthcare professional.
options.D: I’ll share it with a family member who develops similar symptoms if we use the same dose, because similar symptoms usually need the same antibiotic.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. CDC guidance dated September 23, 2025 instructs clients to take antibiotics exactly as prescribed, not share antibiotics, not save them for later, and contact a healthcare professional with questions; CDC also advises contacting a healthcare professional if side effects occur. B is incorrect because the client should not independently change the prescribed duration based only on symptom improvement. C is incorrect because CDC specifically advises against saving antibiotics for a later illness because the wrong medicine may delay correct treatment and cause harm. D is incorrect because CDC advises never sharing antibiotics or taking an antibiotic prescribed for someone else.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach safe antibiotic self-administration: follow the current prescription exactly, do not share or save antibiotics, and involve a healthcare professional rather than independently changing treatment or managing adverse effects.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do's and Don'ts

semantic_correction.source_locator: Take antibiotics exactly as prescribed — take them exactly as prescribed; do not share antibiotics; do not save them for later; do not take antibiotics prescribed for someone else; talk to a healthcare professional with questions. Talk to a healthcare provider about side effects of antibiotics — call a healthcare professional if side effects develop.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends taking antibiotics exactly as prescribed, not sharing them, not saving them for later, not using another person's prescription, and contacting a healthcare professional with questions or side effects.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests safe antibiotic self-administration, corrects the blueprint mapping, and eliminates the uniquely-long correct-answer cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. Every component is directly supported by current CDC antibiotic-use guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Symptom improvement does not authorize the client to independently shorten a prescribed antibiotic regimen; treatment changes should follow professional instructions.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC advises not saving antibiotics for later because a future illness may require a different diagnosis or treatment.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC explicitly advises not sharing antibiotics and not taking medication prescribed for another person.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows current CDC patient-level antibiotic-use guidance; B, C, and D each require a client action that CDC specifically advises against.
cueing_check: The four options are tightly balanced in length (A 150, B 147, C 147, D 148 characters), use parallel first-person statements, and contain no unique formatting or specificity cue favoring A.
